Tests date ranges (ra-tags) of event or episode dates

Source: R/ra_tags.R
date_test_complex.Rd

Tests whether dates lie inside the range that the ra-tag of a date item allows. Typically the range is "between the date of the previous interview and the date of the current interview". The function can test

  • an event: one date (month and year), e.g. the date of a birth, with 7 arguments, or

  • an episode: a start and an end date, e.g. an employment episode, with 9 arguments.

All variables are given as strings. The arguments are positional and always come in month/year pairs: first the two dates that limit the range (pm1/pj1 = lower limit, pm2/pj2 = upper limit), then the date(s) to test (varm1/varj1 = start or event date, varm2/varj2 = end date of an episode).

Usage

date_test_complex(
  data,
  pm1,
  pj1,
  pm2,
  pj2,
  varm1,
  varj1,
  varm2 = NULL,
  varj2 = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A neps field-data dataframe.

pm1, pj1

Month and year variable of the lower limit of the range, e.g. "intmPRE", "intjPRE" (date of the previous interview).

pm2, pj2

Month and year variable of the upper limit of the range, e.g. "intm", "intj" (date of the current interview).

varm1, varj1

Month and year variable of the date to test. For episodes this is the start date, e.g. "ezstm", "ezstj".

varm2, varj2

Month and year variable of the end date of an episode, e.g. "ezendm", "ezendj". Leave out for events.

Value

Prints a success message if all checks pass. Otherwise stops with an error that lists the failed checks and the caseids involved.

Details

Before the comparison, season codes in the month variables (21, 24, 27, 30, 32) are turned into months (1, 4, 7, 10, 12) and NEPS missing codes (-99 to -90, -56 to -51, -29 to -22) are set to NA. Rows in which one of the date variables is NA (i.e. the item was not asked) are dropped.

If only the month is missing (e.g. -97 "verweigert" but a valid year), the date is treated as "some time in that year": January for the earliest and December for the latest possible date. This is the same rule the survey institute uses for the ra-tag checks in the CATI. If the year is missing, the date is not checked.

The function runs up to six checks and reports every failed check with the problematic caseids:

  • p1 > p2: the lower limit lies after the upper limit (should not happen, points to a problem with the preloads).

  • var1 > var2: the episode ends before it starts (episodes only).

  • p1 > var1 / p1 > var2: the start or end date lies before the lower limit.

  • p2 < var1 / p2 < var2: the start or end date lies after the upper limit.

The data needs a caseid variable.

See also

Other test functions: ac_test(), ef_test(), label_test(), value_label_test()

Examples

test_data <- data.frame(
  caseid = c(1, 2),
  intmPRE = c(12, 3), intjPRE = c(2023, 2023), # previous interview
  intm = c(10, 11), intj = c(2024, 2024),      # current interview
  ezstm = c(1, 21), ezstj = c(2024, 2024),     # 21 = Jahresanfang/Winter
  ezendm = c(6, -97), ezendj = c(2024, 2024)   # -97 = verweigert
)

# episode: start and end date must lie between the two interviews
date_test_complex(test_data, "intmPRE", "intjPRE", "intm", "intj",
                  "ezstm", "ezstj", "ezendm", "ezendj")
#> [1] "SUCCESS:: All checks passed successfully."

# event: only one date to test
date_test_complex(test_data, "intmPRE", "intjPRE", "intm", "intj", "ezstm", "ezstj")
#> [1] "SUCCESS:: All checks passed successfully."
